s:
Consider the following statements about NCRB's ADSI 2024 report:
1. It recorded 1,70,746 suicides.
2. Daily wagers formed about 31% of the suicides.
3. Drug-overdose deaths fell by about 50%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: ADSI 2024 recorded 1,70,746 suicides, about 31% of them daily wagers. Statement 3 is wrong: drug-overdose deaths (978) rose by 50%, not fell. So '1 and 2 only'.

s: According to Durkheim, what does anomic suicide result from?
x: Anomic suicide arises from too little regulation; fatalistic suicide from too much regulation.

s: In which year was Durkheim's study 'Le Suicide' published?
x: Durkheim's Le Suicide appeared in 1897.

s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2015, which was the leading cause of farmer suicides in India?

s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2015, which cause ranked second among causes of farmer suicides?
x: Farming-related issues came second after bankruptcy or indebtedness in ADSI 2015.

s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2024, which State recorded the highest number of suicides?
x: Maharashtra recorded the most suicides in 2024 (22,174), followed by Tamil Nadu (19,965) and Madhya Pradesh.

s: What is that crime, which when tried is punishable, but when done the culprit crime doer cannot be punished?
x: When the question was asked Suicide was a crime. Suicide was such a crime that if done, the culprit is not available for punishment. Although its attempt was punishable earlier under section 309 of the IPC. But the Law Commission of India in its 210th report recommended deleting Section 309 of I.P.C. and which was supported by 18 states and 4 Union Territories to delete Section 309 of IPC from the statute book.

s: Which case held Section 309 IPC, punishing attempted suicide, invalid in 1994?
x: P. Rathinam (1994) held Section 309 invalid; Section 309 made attempted suicide punishable with imprisonment up to one year and/or fine.

s: The main cause for poverty of rural and tribal people is?
Who propounded the concept of the “culture of poverty” in 1959?
x: The concept of the “culture of poverty” was propounded by Oscar Lewis in 1959.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the social indicators of poverty?
x: Illiteracy, malnutrition, poor health care and lack of safe water and sanitation are social indicators of poverty; size of the house is not one.

s: What is being poor compared with others in the same society called?
x: Relative poverty means being poor in comparison with others in the same society; absolute poverty is spending below a fixed poverty line.

s: On which of the following is India's official poverty line based?
x: India's official poverty line is consumption-based, set by Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE), not income.

s: Who chaired the Rangarajan Committee, which dealt with poverty measurement?
x: C. Rangarajan chaired the Rangarajan Expert Group (set up 2012, report 2014). Suresh Tendulkar chaired the earlier 2005 group, while S.R. Hashim (urban BPL households) and N.C. Saxena (rural BPL census) headed the 2009 groups.

s: On what calorie requirements was the Y.K. Alagh Committee's poverty estimation method based?
o: 2,700 calories in rural areas and 2,400 calories in urban areas
2,400 calories in rural areas and 2,100 calories in urban areas
2,100 calories in rural areas and 2,400 calories in urban areas
2,200 calories in both rural and urban areas
x: The Y.K. Alagh Committee, formed in 1979, used a calorie norm of 2,400 calories for rural areas and 2,100 calories for urban areas. The corresponding expenditure was treated as the poverty line.

s: Which of the following was a significant departure introduced by the Tendulkar Committee methodology?
o: It used only rural consumption baskets for both sectors.
It excluded non-food expenditure from the poverty line.
It restored the calorie anchor as the sole basis of poverty estimation.
It dropped the calorie anchor and included health and education expenditure.
x: The Tendulkar Committee (report 2009) dropped the calorie anchor, used the Mixed Reference Period (MRP), applied the urban basket to both sectors and included health and education spending. The other options are wrong: it did not use a rural-only basket, exclude non-food spending or restore the calorie anchor.

s: What were the Rangarajan poverty lines for 2011-12?
o: ₹32 per day rural and ₹47 per day urban
₹32 per day urban and ₹47 per day rural
₹47 per day in both rural and urban areas
₹27 per day rural and ₹33 per day urban
x: Rangarajan estimated ₹32 per day for rural and ₹47 per day for urban areas (₹972 and ₹1,407 per month).

s: Which poverty estimation method used CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas?
x: The Lakdawala methodology kept the calorie base, used state-specific poverty lines and applied CPI-AL for rural and CPI-IW for urban areas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.R. Hashim Expert Group – Rural BPL census
N.C. Saxena Expert Group – Rural BPL census methodology
Rangarajan Committee – Chaired by Bimal Jalan
N.C. Saxena Expert Group – Urban BPL households
x: N.C. Saxena dealt with the rural BPL census and S.R. Hashim with urban BPL identification; C. Rangarajan chaired the Rangarajan Committee.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, what was poverty in 2023-24 as measured by the Tendulkar line?
x: Poverty measured by the Tendulkar line was stated to have fallen from 21.9 percent in 2011–12 to 2.3 percent in 2023–24.

s: In which year was the Y.K. Alagh Task Force on poverty estimation set up?
x: The Alagh Task Force (1979) used a calorie-only norm of 2,400 rural and 2,100 urban.

s: According to the Tendulkar methodology, what was poverty in India in 2011-12?
x: The Tendulkar line put poverty at 21.9% in 2011-12; 37.2% was its 2004-05 figure and 2.3% the 2023-24 figure.

s: In October 2025, which body updated the Rangarajan poverty line using HCES 2022-23?
x: In October 2025 the RBI updated the Rangarajan line using HCES 2022-23 and a poverty-line-basket price index.

s: Which expert group included both food and non-food needs such as housing, clothing, education, health and transport in its poverty line?
x: The Rangarajan Expert Group (report 2014) built its poverty line on separate food and non-food needs.

s: In which year was the Tendulkar Expert Group on poverty estimation set up?
x: The Tendulkar Expert Group was set up in 2005 and gave its report in 2009.

s: According to the Tendulkar Expert Group, what was the poverty ratio in India in 2004-05?
x: The Tendulkar method put poverty at 37.2% in 2004-05 and 21.9% in 2011-12.

s: Which expert group's method gave a poverty estimate of 27.5% for 2004-05?
x: The Lakdawala method (state-specific lines with CPI-AL / CPI-IW) gave 27.5% poverty for 2004-05.

s: What were the monthly per capita poverty lines for 2011-12 set by the Rangarajan Expert Group for rural and urban areas respectively?
x: Rangarajan's lines were ₹972 (rural) and ₹1,407 (urban) a month, i.e. about ₹32 and ₹47 a day.

s: Which expert group was set up in 2009 to recommend the method of identifying urban BPL households?
x: The S.R. Hashim group (2009) dealt with urban BPL households; N.C. Saxena dealt with the rural BPL census.

s: Which expert group on poverty adopted the Mixed Reference Period (MRP) and used the urban consumption basket for both rural and urban areas?
x: The Tendulkar group (report 2009) adopted MRP, used the urban basket for both sectors and dropped the calorie anchor.

s:

Who among the following are eligible to benefit from the ‘Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act’?
o: Adult members of only the scheduled caste and
Adult members of Below Poverty Line (BPL)
Adult members of households of all backward
x: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 was passed by the Parliament in August, 2005 and came into force on 2 February, 2006. Its name changed to MNREGA on 2nd October 2009. This programme was started in Anantpur district of Andhra Pradesh. The adult members of any household are eligible for an employment guarantee of at least 100 days. The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) : VB- G RAM G Act, 2025 has received the assent of the President of India on 20th December, 2025. This Act shall come into effect on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaces MGNREGA with a new Statutory framework, aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047. The Act enhances the Employment Guarantee to 125 days per rural household annually, and strengthens income security.

s:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : MGNREGA is providing employment to at least one member of the eligible household for a minimum period of 100 days in a year.
Reason (R) : Right to employment is enumerated in Part III of the Constitution.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
x: "Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA )" is an Indian labour law and social security measure that aims to guarantee the “Right to Work’’. It aims to ensure livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of employment in a financial year to every household whose adult member volunteers to do unskilled manual work. This Act aims to follow the Directive Principles of State Policy.

x: The Gram Sabha's role in the notes is holding social audits, along with recommending works and monitoring them. Receiving applications for work and issuing dated receipts is done by the Gram Panchayat (programme officer), not the Gram Sabha, so option 2 is the answer.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the original MGNREGA guarantee?
o: A legal right to 100 days of unskilled wage work per rural household per year
Payment of unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days
Social audits by the Gram Sabha
Reservation of exactly half of all workdays for women
x: The guarantee required that one-third of workers be women, not exactly half. The 100-day legal guarantee, 15-day unemployment allowance and Gram Sabha social audits are features of MGNREGA.

s: Under MGNREGA, at least what share of the workers must be women?
x: At least one-third of MGNREGA workers must be women, not half.

s: Under MGNREGA, if work is not provided within how many days of demand is an unemployment allowance due?
x: If work is not given within 15 days of demand, an unemployment allowance is payable.

s: NREGA came into force on 2 February 2006, starting in which district?

s:
